payload.outcome: Closed on an owner decision plus a fix, 2026-09-02. Reissued after the reconciliation on main (#2542) applied the other session's update to this row, which made the first attempt's fingerprint stale; the substance is unchanged, and that update's own finding is what this closes. THE SINGULAR HALF was already fixed before the row could be acted on: Ruling [143] on 2026-08-27 put the job-title lookbehind into tests/helpers/caring-contacts-prohibited-language.ts, and ran the fix the opposite way round from what the row anticipates -- the interface definition was the STRICTER of the two, so COMMERCIAL_LEAD_PATTERN in src/lib/caring-contacts/message-rules.ts was tightened to mirror it rather than the reverse. Both examples the row names, 'the incident lead' and 'the clinical programme lead', are permitted on both surfaces. THE PLURAL HALF was real and stayed open, exactly as the applied update established by re-measuring: the bare leads alternative sat ahead of the narrowed branch with no lookbehind, so 'clinical leads', 'programme leads', 'team leads', 'service leads' and 'incident leads' were all refused. That is ordinary English -- 'nobody's job title is plural' is true of one person's title and false of a group of them. One correction to that update, so it is not acted on as written: reusing COMMERCIAL_LEAD_PATTERN was no longer the route, because since Ruling [143] that pattern is term for term identical to the interface helper and carries the same bare leads. Both surfaces had become equally strict, so the row's alternative framing -- record why interface copy should be stricter than message copy -- no longer fitted either. Put to the owner as the decision it had become. DECISION: extend the job-title exemption to the plural ON THE SCREEN ONLY. A screen may now say 'the clinical leads met on Tuesday'; a message to a discharged patient still may not. The asymmetry is the safe direction: loosening patient-visible message wording is the highest-consequence change available in this feature and nothing needed it, and the Ruling [143] parity invariant is one-directional -- it forbids a message permitting what the screen refuses, not the reverse -- so nothing it guards is weakened. IMPLEMENTED as two alternatives mirroring the singular pair: a plural commercial-companion branch ahead of an exempting plural branch, so the exemption cannot license what follows the word it exempts. Commercial plurals untouched: 'sales leads', 'new leads', 'leads capture' and 'clinical leads capture' all still refused. Pinned in BOTH directions by tests/caring-contacts-interface-vocabulary.test.ts -- the screen permits each plural job title AND a message still refuses it -- so a later edit tidying the message side to match goes red. Known residual, measured and filed separately: the plural exemption also permits preceding-verb commercial phrasing such as 'capture clinical leads'. Landed in PR #2521; verified 69 caring-contacts test files, 1479 tests passing.
